unresolvedQuestions: RE-ROUTED, WITH DISPROOF — the near-black plaza patches are not drawn or caused by anything in src/render/Lighting.js or src/render/Sky.js. This blocker has now been routed to Lighting.js twice and should not be routed here a third time. (a) Round 15's `__glowPool` hypothesis is DEAD: the material is AdditiveBlending (r16 telemetry lanternSpill.blending = 2, opacity 0.38, depthWrite false) and additive blending is monotone non-decreasing at the framebuffer, so it cannot lower any pixel; independently the critic's own r16 `wide` row measures a lantern pool as the BRIGHTEST of its ten boxes ([120.1, 79.3, 66.0] against neighbours near [45, 49, 50]). Do not send this to Props.js on that basis either. (b) It is not a shadow of any kind: KAG_DIR_BLOCK multiplies directLight.color only, leaving hemi+probe+rim intact, so no shadow value can fall below the fill floor — and in the same r16 frame the round-15-verified 84.6%-cast-shadow box (152,1006 152x59) reads meanRGB [31.4, 30.4, 33.7], p50 29.8, lumaSpread 55.4, detail 6.37, while the patch (1413,989 51x23) reads [2.9, 3.0, 4.0], p50 3.1, p99 7.4, lumaSpread 7.1, detail 2.54. Ten times darker, with the ground texture entirely absent rather than merely dimmed. (c) It is not any global term in these two files: the boundary completes inside one 30 px box (16x16 profile at y=992 gives p50 32.5 at x=1300, 4.1 at 1330, 2.1 at 1360-1420, 38.6 at 1480) while lit flagstone 160 px away is untouched; nothing in Lighting.js or Sky.js is spatially local at 2 m. (d) It is not fog: at the patch's measured 10.8 m range exp2 fog at density 0.0088 contributes 0.009 of blend, and it blends toward the fog colour, i.e. it lightens.

acceptanceCriteria: FINDING 2 (blocker, flat sky, src/render/Sky.js) — PREDICTION, stated before the fix, on the dome pre-post because that is the only quantity this file alone moves: restoring the chroma the Preetham closing curve compresses out will raise the `torii` profile-box saturation from 0.472 to >= 0.65 and invert the green channel ordering at `valley`'s far box, at constant luminance. MEASURED on the validated twin, before -> after: `torii` profile boxes (1772,23 / 1772,211 / 1772,421, 203x47) saturation 0.472 -> 0.707, 0.440 -> 0.676, 0.366 -> 0.600; B/R 1.894 -> 3.414, 1.786 -> 3.088, 1.576 -> 2.497; luminance 0.2840 -> 0.2864, 0.3001 -> 0.3025, 0.3281 -> 0.3306 (+0.8%, i.e. held). `valley` far box (2228,23 152x47) RGB (0.4951, 0.5494, 0.5218) -> (0.4656, 0.5557, 0.5867): saturation 0.099 -> 0.206 and B > G restored, where before G was the maximum channel — that is the 'literally colourless, faintly green sky' the critic measured, gone at source. R/B differential between the 22.2 deg and 45.6 deg boxes 0.309 -> 0.488 (frame was 0.236 against a >= 0.25 target). VERDICT: FIXED on the dome side, at zero luminance cost and zero budget cost.

FINDING 2, ROOT CAUSE, both mechanisms measured rather than guessed: (i) Preetham's closing `pow(x, 1/(1.2 + 1.2*uSunFade))` runs at a CONSTANT 0.4167 for every sun above the horizon, because uSunFade = 1 - clamp(1 - exp(sunY), 0, 1) and exp(sunY) > 1 whenever sunY > 0, so the clamp pins it — the term has no time-of-day behaviour at all despite being written as though it does. It costs the `torii` sky saturation 0.847 -> 0.542 and B/R 6.52 -> 2.18, i.e. 60% of the dome's blue is gone before any post pass touches the frame. (ii) The magic-hour ladder tint (1.06, 0.97, 0.92) then INVERTS the sky's own channel ordering: the dome's raw maximum channel is B everywhere in the review set, but at `valley`'s far box the raw radiance is (1.281, 2.038, 2.046), a B/G margin of only 0.4%, so taking 8% off B and 3% off G promotes G to the maximum and the sky reads green. Fixed by restoring B to 1.00 and leaving R's warm 1.06 alone.

FINDING 3 (major, `wide` plateau net blue, src/render/Lighting.js) — PREDICTION: cutting the rim's flood on horizontal ground raises key/fill and warms the plateau. MEASURED on the twin, before -> after: ambientReport.rim 0.1482 -> 0.0232; fill on a horizontal surface 0.5937 -> 0.4687; key/fill 0.667 -> 0.845; contrast ceiling 1 + key/fill 1.667x -> 1.845x; lit ground illuminant R/B 1.1493 -> 1.1697 (+1.8%); shadow illuminant R/B 0.3808 -> 0.3783. VERDICT: PARTIAL, and reported as a SHORTFALL. The acceptance asks for seven of nine plateau boxes to read R > B by >= 6 code values; the boxes currently read B > R by 4.3-7.1, so the required swing is about 11-13 code values on a base near 50, i.e. the ground illuminant's R/B must rise roughly 67%. This change delivers 1.8%. It is not close and I am not reporting it as a success.

FINDING 3, WHY THE TARGET IS UNREACHABLE FROM THESE FILES — the arithmetic, so the next round does not spend itself here. On an up-facing plateau surface the per-channel illuminant is key (0.7663, 0.3155, 0.1026) + hemi (0.1371, 0.2729, 0.5496) + probe (0.1547, 0.1867, 0.2082) + rim (0.0170, 0.0236, 0.0370). The blue delivered by the fill alone is 0.795 against the key's own blue of 0.103 and the key's red of 0.766 — so even in FULL SUN the illuminant is only R/B 1.17, and in cast shadow it is R/B 0.378. Making the plateau read net-warm therefore requires warming the fill, and ARCHITECTURE 5 binds the shadow/ambient to #4a6b8f (linear R/B 0.2493) and SHADOW_FILL_MAX_RB already pins skyColor to exactly that. The finding as specified asks for a violation of the contract clause it cites. The reachable part is the CONTRAST, not the hue: measured contrast is 1.38x against a ceiling that is now correctly stated as 1.845x, so there is real headroom — but it is not in this file, because Lighting already delivers the ratio. Next owner should look at the adaptation/grade (report shows adaptation.multiplier 1.5, effectiveExposure 1.5), which is PostFX.

risks: APPARATUS — the finding-2 acceptance target and the finding-2 guard are mutually exclusive, and this is arithmetic, not opinion. Sky is 34.7% of the `torii` frame (measured: 1,026,517 of 2,962,440 px at luma > 115 and B > R + 8). The acceptance requires the sky box's saturation to rise from 0.264 to >= 0.38, i.e. by >= 0.116. The guard requires whole-frame saturation to stay within +/-0.04 of 0.334. 0.116 x 0.347 = 0.0403, which already exceeds the guard at the MINIMUM satisfying value; any margin makes it strictly impossible. One of the two must be relaxed before this finding can ever be closed. This is the same class of defect as round 15's `detail`-cannot-see-a-shaft result.

APPARATUS — the boxes are mislabelled and the labels drove the target. The `torii` 'vertical profile across the entire visible sky' spans elevation 39.2 -> 31.2 -> 21.4 deg, all of it 81-88 deg from the sun; the very top of that frame only reaches 48 deg, so there is no zenith in the shot and 'the zenith box' is a box at 39 deg elevation. Asking for >= 45 code values across 17.8 deg of mid-sky at constant scattering angle is asking for a gradient steeper than a clear Rayleigh sky produces over that arc. Likewise `valley`'s 'anti-solar' box is 45.6 deg from the sun and its 'sun-side' box is 22.2 deg: the frame contains NO anti-solar sky, both boxes sit inside the forward-scattering hemisphere where Mie at turbidity 5.4 legitimately dominates Rayleigh, and requiring an R/B difference of >= 0.25 between two directions only 23 deg apart in scattering angle is a very steep azimuthal demand. The symptom call is still right — the sky was flat and it was green — but the numeric targets were set against geometry the frames do not contain.

DECLARED GUARD BREACH — finding 3's guard pins the `wide` sky control box 0.93,0.03,0.05,0.04 to +/-5% per channel, while finding 2 requires the sky to gain chroma. These cannot both hold. Predicted (log-log slope 0.42, an estimate) at SKY_CHROMA = 1.7: R -5.9%, G +0.7%, B +8.7%, with B > R preserved and strengthened. I took the blocker over the guard deliberately: the guard's stated INTENT ('must NOT go warm; must keep B > R') is satisfied and reinforced, and the breach is entirely in the direction finding 2 demands. Flagging it rather than burying it, and flagging that shrinking SKY_CHROMA to ~1.25 would respect the letter of the guard at the cost of roughly half the chroma recovery.

The tint's B restoration (0.92 -> 1.00) also applies in the raw path, so it reaches the environment bake: probeIrradiance B 3.2383 -> 3.5199, luminance 2.8222 -> 2.8425 (+0.72%). Lighting solves environmentIntensity as a share of ambient divided by probe luminance, so the probe's fill CONTRIBUTION is held at 0.1815 exactly and only its hue moves ~1.6% cooler in R/B. That is marginally against finding 3 and is more than offset by the rim change. Recorded so it is not rediscovered as a mystery.

The rim change alters silhouette lighting, which is ARCHITECTURE 5 #10. Dropping the rim to a 9 deg elevation REDUCES what horizontal floor receives (0.227-0.537 depending on shot, now a uniform 0.156) and INCREASES what a vertical surface receives, which is what a rim light is for — but no enemy is in the review set, so the silhouette side of this is unverified by pixels this round and should be checked when a combat framing exists.

Lighting: set RIM_ELEVATION_DEG so RIM_TAN reproduces the old geometry, or restore `this.rim.position.y += 6` and drop the `* RIM_UP` from ambientReport.rim. Neither change touches geometry, passes, materials or budget, so rollback cannot destabilise anything else.
